options.text: In Ukraine, the United States invaded with ground troops, as it had in Iraq
options.misconception: The United States did not send ground troops to fight in Ukraine.

options.text: In Ukraine, the United States took no action at all
options.misconception: The United States condemned the invasion, imposed sanctions, and sent military aid.

options.text: In Iraq, the United States imposed sanctions but sent no troops
options.misconception: The United States invaded Iraq with ground troops in 2003.

options.text: In Ukraine, the United States backed the invaded country with aid and sanctions

rationales.A: The United States sent military aid to Ukraine, not ground troops to fight there.
rationales.B: Sanctions and military aid are real actions. The United States did not stand aside.
rationales.C: Background: the United States invaded Iraq with ground troops in March 2003. Sanctions alone do not describe that war.
rationales.D: The account says the United States condemned the invasion, imposed sanctions, and gave Ukraine over 64 billion dollars in military aid by 2025.
rationales.general:
1. Compare the two responses on one measure: American troops. Background: in Iraq in 2003, the United States invaded with its own forces.
2. In Ukraine in 2022, the United States sent aid to the country that was invaded and imposed sanctions on Russia.
3. Backing an invaded country with aid is the opposite of invading a country yourself.
4. The difference is the role: invader in one case, supporter in the other.
Remember: aid and sanctions support an ally, while an invasion puts your own troops on the ground.

stimulus.source_note: Photograph: official White House photograph, September 2020. Public domain (U.S. federal government work). Account paraphrased from the grounding books (Barron's Premium 2027 Ch. 11, Topic 9.6; 5 Steps 2024 Ch. 31).
stimulus.text:
Photograph of the Abraham Accords signing ceremony at the White House in September 2020: President Donald Trump, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel, and the foreign ministers of the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain sit at a table outdoors, signing documents.

Paraphrase of a secondary account: In 2020, the Trump administration mediated the Abraham Accords, agreements in which the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain normalized relations with Israel. Trump had earlier moved the American embassy in Israel to Jerusalem in 2018 and withdrawn the United States from the Iran nuclear deal, the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action, in the same year. In 2022, Russia invaded Ukraine, and the United States under President Biden condemned the invasion, imposed sanctions, and had given Ukraine over 64 billion dollars in military aid by 2025.
